A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Spectral-Refiner study and contain the main text and Appendices A–E. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, figures, tables and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original Taylor-Green vortex and isotropic-turbulence experiments, including accuracy, runtime, ablation and distribution-shift results in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their numerical and graphical results in Section 4 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The ST-FNO architecture, spectral fine-tuning objective and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. Correcting the single-step/multistep solver description and identifying the solver as IMEX clarify documentation without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Taylor-Green vortex, forced turbulence and McWilliams decaying turbulence, including the same shifted initial-energy distributions and Reynolds-number scenarios in Appendix D.4.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1, 3 and 6 and Figure 13, including PS+RK2, FNO3d, IMEX Runge-Kutta and FNO(2+1)d rollout. Newly cited neural operators are not added to the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices C–D retain the same data splits, grid resolutions, temporal sampling, training budgets, model configurations and metrics. The added IMEX identification does not document a revised experimental setting or rerun.

E4.justification: The loss-function ablations, residual visualizations, padding illustration, spectral-convergence analyses and distribution-shift tests are retained. Tables 2–3 and 7 and Figures 5–13 introduce no new analytical questions or evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same fixed seed in Appendix D.1, 20 runtime measurements in Table 6, and ten training seeds with error bars showing ten times the standard deviation in Figure 8. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The reported numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains the fine-tuned L2 error of 2.88 × 10^-4, and Table 7 retains the Reynolds-number-10,000 failure with fine-tuned error 2.355 × 10^6.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, error bounds and norm equivalence in Sections 2–3, derivations in Appendices B–C, and assumptions and proofs in Appendix E are retained. No mathematical correction or new theoretical result is introduced.

C1.justification: The claims about temporal super-resolution, spectral fine-tuning, negative-Sobolev loss and accuracy remain the same. The revised contribution bullet's 'for the first time' wording repeats novelty already asserted in v2's abstract and Section 3.2.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the functional-norm motivation, sufficient-closeness qualifications, restriction to FNO-based architectures and interpretation of the failed high-Reynolds-number experiment. The solver clarification introduces no substantive new limitation or mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 now explicitly identifies the fine-tuning solver as implicit-explicit, and Appendix B attributes its selection to Wang & Liu (2002) and Wang (2012). This adds implementation provenance; the hyperparameters, hardware and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds eight cited works covering neural operators, fluid modeling and numerical solvers, including Transolver, Prometheus and Wang & Liu (2002), without substantially changing the paper's positioning. The FNO citation's 2020-to-2021 update refers to the same work.

P1.justification: Limited edits revise contribution bullets, correctly distinguish single-step RK4 from multistep solvers, clarify solver terminology and remove wording errors such as duplicated 'dealiasing.' The section organization and overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 and Table 2 receive citation-year updates, while the expanded bibliography and Appendix B cause local page reflow. All thirteen figures and seven tables retain their graphics, axes, legends and structures.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects v2's classification of RK4 as a multistep solver, makes the fine-tuning solver's identity and provenance clearer, and modestly expands relevant literature coverage. These improve technical clarity and traceability. The experiments, results, theory and substantive limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
